title: Thrift: Compact protocol dissector
description: [Apache Thrift](https://thrift.apache.org) defines several different protocols for encoding data. Wireshark already has a dissector for the "Binary" protocol; this MR adds support for the "Compact" protocol.

notes.body: really need ?

My thinking here went something along these lines:

* Although I was dealing with a "compact protocol" capture over UDP, I was surprised not to be offered the option to "Dissect as ... Thrift".
* I solved that by adding `dissector_add_uint("udp.port", 0, thrift_handle);`.
* I figured the same should apply to TCP, so did the same thing, though was unable to test it, not having a suitable capture.

It may well be wrong - what do you think?

sure, sorry. Here is one: [thrift-compact.pcap.gz](/uploads/f653e5ba43a48940e7cc741e6e7de0c6/thrift-compact.pcap.gz)

The data in the capture is from [Jaeger](https://www.jaegertracing.io).

I would have thought about something like that:
```C
dissector_add_for_decode_as_with_preference("udp.port", thrift_handle);
```
Although doing that seems that we might have a conflict between binary & compact protocols (or binary takes tcp, compact takes udp or something similar).

I'm currently working on the binary protocol dissection (for #16244) or rather waiting for legal dept. to clear my code for contribution.

I'll look into a way to merge properly both decoders and have a single handle for binary and compact.

In any case, if this is the only thing that bothers you regarding this PR, I suggest you accept and keep that point in mind for my PR as I rewrote big parts of the decoder and did some improvements in the registration as well.

This will help me proceed with the merge using current code from Richard (including the UDP handling).

After a quick-and-extremely-dirty merge, I got the patch to work on my branch and I saw a notable difference between the way Thrift Binary & Compact protocols are displayed.
Binary shows something like that for structures:
```text
- Struct
  + Type 1
  + Field Id 1
  + Value 1
  + Type 2
  + Field Id 2
  + Value 2
  + Stop
```
while this implementation for compact protocol shows something like that:
```text
- Struct
  - Member 1
    + Type 1
    + Field Id 1
    + Value 1
  - Member 2
    + Type 2
    + Field Id 2
    + Value 2
```
While I understand the possible readability issues (I had some doubts about the way it is done for binary protocol at first), in the compact case the number of sub-tree level can go wild pretty quickly (I counted 14 levels in your example).

So my question is: Is this additional sub-tree an hard requirement for you or would you be OK for more consistency between the 2 displays?

The idea is that if, during the merge, I align compact with binary, it will be easier to apply the improvements than first aligning binary with compact while maintaining the level of improvements.

Last point is that the sub-dissector make the display cleaner as we can hide the type and field id because we directly have the name of the member. Obviously, sub-dissector would have the same effect for compact protocol.

Hi Triton, thanks very much for taking a look at my MR!

Firstly, I absolutely think that the compact and binary dissectors should be consistent. After all, they are really just different encodings of the same data. When I was writing this compact dissector, I couldn't (easily) find a capture of the binary protocol to compare with, so I couldn't really tell if what I was doing was consistent or not.

I agree that we can end up with a crazy number of subtrees, and I'm not particularly tied to that style. It seemed a bit more readable for large structures, but :shrug: 

Another approach might be something like:

```
- Struct
  + Field Id 1 (Type 1): Value 1
  + Field Id 2 (Type 2): Value 2
  + Stop
```

... but then you can't see which bytes in the capture correspond to the Field ID and Type. (Maybe we could have a way of switching between the two formats?)

Hi Richard, at least we agree on the consistency need and I had the exact same issue (not having compact capture, which is now fixed thanks to the jaeger capture).

My proposal is to continue with your MR as it is as to bring the compact part to everyone as soon as possible.
The merge of both will be quite huge anyway and as I said I need to wait for legal before I can open my own PR.
I don't see the merge as an additional delay as we don't use compact internally so there is no risk whatsoever regarding IP.

I hope I'll be able to publish one capture for binary protocol (once again, under review right now).

Now, regarding your proposal, it looks like a lot of work to display it like that instead of using the standard hf_info things. I think that the sub-dissector is the way to go for that. In any case, I agree with the potential readability issue so let's see how we can work that out.

If you look at current code, you might see the `show_internal_thrift_fields` variable which is fixed.
What I did was to leverage it as a preference “Whether the Thrift dissector should display Thrift internal fields for sub-dissectors.”

The examples below show exactly how my current implementation works.
For generic dissection, we always have the internal fields:
```text
- Struct
  + Type: T_I32
  + Field id: 1
  + Integer32: 6
```
And for sub-dissectors, we actually have the choice of activating:
```text
- Invalid Parameter Error
  + Type: T_I32
  + Field id: 1
  + Generic Error Code: Invalid parameter name (6)
```
or not
```text
- Invalid Parameter Error
  + Generic Error Code: Invalid parameter name (6)
```

This way, we get several things:
* We always are able to pinpoint the displayed element (if you select the "Invalid parameter name" line, you will see 00000006 (or just 06 for compact) highlighted.
* With the generic dissector, the users are able to follow their html documentation to go from field to field.
* With a sub-dissector, the users are able to see only the useful data (once written and tested, we can consider that the sub-dissector will not mis-interprete the binary stream).
* Display between generic dissector and sub-dissector is consistent (and in the case of sub-dissector without internal fields, the additional sub-tree does not bring anything).

One more thing, I'm also thinking about generating the sub-dissector from the `.thrift` files, even if it's clearly not for the short term.

Do you think this would bring more pros than cons ('cause obviously, we can only weight the pros and cons for each as none of the proposed solutions are perfect)?

Hi Triton, that sounds like a very sensible approach to me.

I also wasn't able to find any examples of thrift sub-dissectors so again, wasn't able to see how that side was meant to work. I really hope you're able to get legal signoff so you can share your work here.

Long-term, I love the idea of being able to generate the sub-dissectors from the `.thrift` files.

Honestly, I had to ask Anders for the sub-dissector example. :)

Only then was I able to understand and update this part as well to be able to handle pretty much anything as it was not the case yet (missing containers in particular).

I'll provide the example as well and already requested the access rights for the wiki for that.

It's just a matter of time, to do things right:
* I have the `.thrift` files
* I have an associated capture (complete enough to cover all kinds of cases)
* I need to finish the sub-dissector example (not difficult but long due to manual process)
* Then the documentation can be written based on the example

Regarding compact protocol, we can do the same with the jaeger capture, only 2 of the `.thrift` files from the project are necessary, `jaeger.thrift` and `agent.thrift`. It’s small enough to be doable manually while complete enough to show all kinds of cases.

In any case, if done right, the compact sub-dissector should look the same as the binary sub-dissector, except with `dissect_thrift_c_struct` instead of `dissect_thrift_t_struct`.

@richvdh If you want this to be merged, I think you need to rebase first otherwise it will not be “eligible”.

Maybe also replace all the `dissector_add_uint()` calls with 
```
dissector_add_for_decode_as_with_preference("udp.port", thrift_handle_udp);
```
and if everything works fine for you, it should allow the merge.

This way, I’ll be much more at ease with the merge (knowing your code is accepted makes it easier to build on it).

@AndersBroman : would you prefer I fix the warnings in this branch, or leave it to @EnigmaTriton to fix as part of his larger work in !3598?

I'd say leave it to me as I'm pretty much rewriting most of it to handle the sub-dissection as well. :)

If you can live with your build until the merge of our work is on master, it would probably be less work for everyone.

Note: I also found a bug in the handling of i16. You treat it as fixed 2-bytes field while it is encoded as a zigzag varint according to https://github.com/apache/thrift/blob/master/doc/specs/thrift-compact-protocol.md (confirmed with the C# serializer & fixed on my side).

It appears that this implementation does not follow the TCompactProtocol "real spec" so this MR should probably be closed and not merged anyway.

I just found that the specification at https://github.com/apache/thrift/blob/master/doc/specs/thrift-compact-protocol.md is incorrect as stated in https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/THRIFT-5300. Even though the issue in the specs was found, no update was done and this implementation follow the written but incorrect specifications.

This was not found in the provided test case (Jaeger) because the only collections used are list of structs and structs are one of the few type whose respective values in TBinaryProtocol and TCompactProtocol are equal.

I opened an MR on Thrift documentation (https://github.com/apache/thrift/pull/2417) and will update the dissector accordingly.
